Ball 1 starts in position 1. In that position it is ejected only if piston 1 fires (probability 1⁄3); otherwise (probability 2⁄3) it simply rolls away.  So E₁ = 1⁄3.

Ball 2 starts in position 2.  If piston 2 fires (1⁄3) it is ejected; otherwise (2⁄3) it moves to position 1 and then has chance E₁.  Thus
E₂ = (1⁄3)·1 + (2⁄3)·E₁ = 1⁄3 + (2⁄3)(1⁄3) = 5⁄9.

Any ball that first appears in position 3 (ball 3 and every higher-numbered ball) obeys:
• piston 3 fires (1⁄3) → ejected;
• piston 2 fires (1⁄3) → jumps to position 1 → chance E₁;
• piston 1 fires (1⁄3) → moves to position 2 → chance E₂.
Hence
E₃ = (1⁄3)·1 + (1⁄3)·E₁ + (1⁄3)·E₂
     = 1⁄3 + 1⁄9 + 5⁄27 = 17⁄27 ≈ 0.63.

Thus P(ejection) for ball 1 = 1⁄3 < ball 2 = 5⁄9 < ball 3 (and every later ball) = 17⁄27.  All balls from 3 to 100 are equally best, so choose the lowest such number: 3.
Let p0, p1, p2 … be the probability that a ball now in position 1, 2, 3, … will eventually be struck by a piston (ejected) rather than just “released.”  

Step dynamics
• With probability 1/3 the first piston fires → the head ball (position 1) is ejected and every other ball shifts forward one place.  
• With probability 2/3 one of the other two pistons fires → the head ball is released and two balls are removed (the struck ball plus the released one); every remaining ball shifts forward two places.

Hence for n ≥ 2 (positions ≥ 3)  
 p(n) = (1/3)·p(n−1) + (2/3)·p(n−2)  (1)
with base values  
 p(0) = 1/3  (only a 1⁄3 chance the head ball is struck)  
 p(1) = 5/9  (easy to check directly)

Using (1):  
p(2)=17/27≈0.62963  
p(3)=47/81≈0.58025  
p(4)=149/243≈0.61317  
p(5)=431/729≈0.59190  
p(6)=0.60614 …

The sequence oscillates while converging toward the long-run mean 3/5=0.6, so its maximum value is p(2)=17/27 attained at position 3.  All later values stay below this peak.

Therefore the ball that starts in position 3—the one numbered 3—is the most likely to be ejected by a piston, giving the greatest chance to win.
